sections.h2: Where is Batavia, and how does it compare with its neighbors?
sections.html:
Batavia is a city on the Fox River in the western Chicago suburbs, mainly in Kane County with a part in DuPage County. It forms the Tri-City area with St. Charles and Geneva, three western suburbs of similar size.

The 2020 census counted 26,098 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,586, up 0.3% from the 2020 base. The city covers 10.62 square miles of land, with 2,458 people per square mile in 2020.

sections.h2: Why is Batavia called the Windmill City?
sections.html:
Batavia was settled in 1833 and is the oldest city in Kane County. It was first called Big Woods, and a local judge renamed it in 1840 after his former home in Batavia, New York. The city was incorporated on July 27, 1872.

In the late nineteenth century it was home to six American-style windmill manufacturers, and into the early twentieth century most of the windmill-powered water pumps on American farms came from three companies there. Many of the limestone factory buildings still stand and now serve as government and commercial offices and storefronts. The Aurora Elgin and Chicago Railway built a power plant in southern Batavia and added a branch to the city in 1902, and the Campana factory, built in 1936 to make cosmetics including Italian Balm, is another landmark.

That history leaves a mix of older houses near the river and newer subdivisions farther out, so pricing a Batavia house starts with its age and block.

sections.h2: What jobs and employers shape Batavia's housing market?
sections.html:
Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, a federal high-energy physics laboratory where the bottom and top quarks were first detected, sits just east of the city limits, and many residents work there. Aldi, Inc., the U.S. subsidiary of Aldi Süd, has its headquarters in Batavia.

Census figures for 2022 show $466.2 million in retail sales, $120.5 million in transportation and warehousing receipts and $108.6 million in health care and social assistance receipts. About 69.0% of residents aged 16 and over are in the labor force, and the mean commute is 28.9 minutes. The Census Bureau lists 5.8% of residents as foreign-born.

sections.h2: How is Batavia governed, and which schools serve it?
sections.html:
The city council has 14 members. Seven wards each elect two aldermen, and the mayor chairs the council and is elected citywide every four years.

  • Batavia Public School District 101 has six K-5 elementary schools, one 6-8 middle school and Batavia High School.
  • Small pockets of the city belong to Geneva Community Unit School District 304 and to West Aurora District 129.
  • The Batavia Public Library District, founded in April 1881 as a township library, serves most of Batavia Township and parts of nearby townships, and its current building opened in January 2002.

Because the district line can follow a street instead of a city boundary, confirm the school assignment for your address before you repeat a school claim in a listing.

sections.h2: What are the main roads and transit options in Batavia?
sections.html:
Batavia Avenue is Illinois Route 31, Main Street is Route 10 and Washington and River streets carry Illinois Route 25 along the river. Randall Road and Wilson Street are also major streets.

Pace operates some bus service, and the Geneva and Aurora Metra stations are nearby. Paths for biking and walking run along the Fox River. Two railroad lines, the Chicago & North Western Aurora Branch and the Burlington Route West Chicago line, served the city directly until 1943, and today a buyer who commutes by train will ask how far the house is from the nearest platform.

  • Check your house's distance to Route 31 or Randall Road, since buyers weigh traffic and access.
  • Mention river-path access if it is within walking distance.

sections.h2: Which county handles my deed and property record in Batavia?
sections.html:
Most of the city lies in Kane County, whose government offices are at 719 Batavia Avenue, Building A, in Geneva, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, though some offices keep different hours. A portion of Batavia lies in DuPage County, so look at the parcel number on your tax bill to see which county's recorder and treasurer apply.

The Illinois Department of Revenue states that the county recorder sells the revenue stamps that pay the state transfer tax. Buyer and seller complete Form PTAX-203, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, and file it in the county where the property is located. A county may also impose 25 cents per $500 of value, and home rule municipalities can add a tax of their own, so ask your title company whether the city does.

Call the recorder's office in your county for its current fee schedule before closing day.

sections.h2: When does selling a Batavia house for cash make sense?
sections.html:
An as-is cash sale suits a house that needs updates, an inherited property, or a seller who must move quickly. A traditional listing suits a house that is ready to show in a market where owner-occupied homes are the norm.

  • Get the offer in writing and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, fees and carrying costs.
  • Confirm how soon the buyer can close and who pays title and recording costs.
  • Keep your tax bill, payoff statement and any permit records together for the title company.

faqs.q: Is Batavia in Kane County or DuPage County?
faqs.a: Mostly Kane County, with a part in DuPage County. The parcel number on your tax bill tells you which county records your deed and collects your property tax.

Batavia Public School District 101 serves most of the city. Small pockets belong to Geneva Community Unit School District 304 and West Aurora School District 129, so verify the district for your address.
It is the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration. The buyer and seller complete it and file it with the county where the property sits when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Batavia house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is, and a cash offer is priced with the condition in mind. Get the terms in writing and compare the net amount with a listing.

The sale contract decides. The state tax is paid through revenue stamps sold by the county recorder, and a county or home rule municipality may add its own tax. Your title company can itemize each charge.
